newsitem.title: USA: U.S. to close embassy in Brazzaville.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to close embassy in Brazzaville.

text.p: The United States said on Tuesday it was temporarily closing its embassy in Brazzaville and would pull out its remaining embassy staff on Wednesday.
"We simply can't protect them any more given the deteriorating security situation," State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns told reporters.
Burns said the U.S. ambassador in Brazzaville had just reported that an international mediation committee had managed to "convince the factional leaders today to agree to a three-day truce".

"We'd like to see this truce implemented. We'd like to see the fighting stop completely," he said, complimenting the representatives of Gabon, France, Mali, Equatorial Guinea as well as the U.S. ambassador for helping bring it about.

Fighting under way in the Congo Republic since June 5 has derailed plans for a July 27 presidential election. Burns said the danger for U.S. personnel was increasing partly because French forces were pulling out.

He said Washington was not severing diplomatic relations with Congo and was not closing the embassy permanently. Local employees would look after the embassy. He said the 12 embassy staff, including the ambassador, two Peace Corps workers and a 12-member U.S. military team would fly out on Wednesday morning from Brazzaville airport.
